712793.t: Possibly from the stem *kʷern̥t- of Proto-Indo-European *kwéronts, active participle of *kʷéreti (“to do, make, perform (magic, etc.)”), thematic variant of *kʷért, in any case from the root *kʷer-, or formed within Greek from a lost verb *τέρω (*térō) +…

712787.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʷélos, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷél-os ~ *kʷél-es-. See Latin colō for more.

712750.t: Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *dʰn̥gʰ-ú-s, zero-grade u-stem of *dʰengʰ- (“to go quickly”), based on the comparison with Lithuanian déngti (“to run, hurry”) (see there for more potential cognates), though Fraenkel has disputed the connection.

712734.t: From Proto-Hellenic *táuros, from Proto-Indo-European *táwros; cognates include Latin taurus, Lithuanian taũras, Old English stēor (English steer), and Albanian ter.

712766.t: From Proto-Hellenic *téktōn, from Proto-Indo-European *tétḱō (“carpenter”), from *tetḱ- (“to create, produce”). Cognate with Sanskrit तक्षन् (tákṣan).

712738.t: From θάπτω (thắptō, “to bury”), particularly from the aorist stem ταφ- (tăph-) with its metathesis of the aspiration.

712791.t: For earlier τάμνω (támnō), with ε (e) from aorist ἔτεμον (étemon), from Proto-Indo-European *tm̥-né-h₁-ti, *tm̥-n-h₁-énti, nasal-infixed present (the present tense system includes a N progressive aspect marker) from *temh₁- (“to cut”).

712751.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʷe, from Proto-Indo-European *-kʷe (“and”). Cognates include Mycenaean Greek 𐀤 (qe), Phrygian κε (ke), Sanskrit च (ca), and Latin -que.

712754.t: From Proto-Hellenic *téňňō, from Proto-Indo-European *tén-ye-ti, the innovative ye-present of *ten- (“stretch”) (The present tense system includes a *y progressive aspect marker).

712761.t: From Proto-Hellenic *téknon, from Proto-Indo-European *teḱ-, perhaps via τίκτω (tíktō, “I bear”). Cognates include Old English þegn (“servant”), Old High German degan and possibly Sanskrit तोक (toka, “offspring, child”).

712759.t: From Proto-Hellenic *téikʰos, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeyǵʰ- (“to knead, form, fashion”). Cognates include Sanskrit देह (deha), Avestan 𐬛𐬀𐬉𐬰𐬀 (daēza, “wall”), Latin fingō, and Old Armenian դէզ (dēz).

712701.t: A nominal formation from ταμεῖν (tămeîn, “to cut up; to divide”), active aorist infinitive of τέμνω (témnō, “to cut; to hew”), though the exact morphological details are unclear; by surface analysis, τέμνω (témnō) + -ίας (-ĭ́ās).

712712.t: From τάσσω (tắssō, “I arrange”, “I order”, aorist passive participial stem: ταγ-, tag-) + -σις (-sĭs).

712730.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *teh₂g-der. Proto-Hellenic *tat͏̌t͏̌ō Ancient Greek τάσσω From Proto-Hellenic *tat͏̌t͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *teh₂g- (“to order, to establish, to rule”).

712742.t: Neuter accusative plural of ταχύς (tăkhŭ́s, “quick”) used as adverb.

712783.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *kʷelh₁- Proto-Hellenic *kʷélos Ancient Greek τέλος (télos) Proto-Indo-European *-yoh₂ Proto-Hellenic *-yō Ancient Greek *-ϳω (*-jō) Ancient Greek τελέω From τέλος (télos, “end”) + *-ϳω (*-jō, denominative verbal suffix).

712725.t: Possibly related to ταρχύω (tărkhū́ō, “to bury solemnly”)

712741.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dʰembʰ-; compare Old Armenian դամբան (damban, “tomb”).

712790.t: From Proto-Hellenic *témenos, from Proto-Indo-European *témh₁nos, from *temh₁- (“to cut”); whence τέμνω (témnō, “I cut”). Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀳𐀕𐀜 (te-me-no).

712769.t: From τέλος (télos, “end”) + -ιος (-ios, adjective suffix). Related to, and largely synonymous with, τελήεις (telḗeis).

712779.t: From τέλος (télos, “aim, purpose”) + -τή (-tḗ), probably formed by analogy with γενετή (genetḗ, “the hour of birth”) from γένος (génos, “kin”).

712757.t: From τεῖχος (teîkhos, “wall, fortification”) + -ίζω (-ĭ́zō, suffix used to form verbs from nouns, adjectives and other verbs).

712714.t: Has been connected with Old Norse þefja (“to stamp”) and þóf (“crowd”) but this theory is not convincing. Probably from Pre-Greek.

712721.t: Uncertain. Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰreh₂gʰ- (“to confuse, agitate, disturb”).

712752.t: From Proto-Hellenic *(s)tégos, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tégos, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)teg- (“roof”). Cognates include Latin tegō (“to cover”), German Decke (“roof”), English thatch.

712722.t: From ταράσσω (tărắssō, “to disturb; to stir; to agitate”) + -ή (-ḗ).

712792.t: Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *ten- (“to stretch”); related to τείνω (teínō, “to stretch”). Cognate with Serbo-Croatian тѐтива, Slovene tetiva (< Proto-Slavic *tętiva), Polish ścięgno.

712768.t: From Proto-Indo-European *telh₂- (“to bear”) + -μων (-mōn), as its original meaning was "bearer".

712798.t: Unknown, related to τέρμινθος (términthos). The form was perhaps influenced by ἐρέβινθος (erébinthos, “chickpea”).
